description: During an active incident, the technical team, legal team, and leadership each need different updates, and the facts are evolving quickly enough that message consistency is becoming difficult.

user_profile.persona: 42-year-old security program manager acting as a communication bridge during incidents
user_profile.context: Everyone wants updates now, but each audience needs a different framing and level of certainty
user_profile.communication_style: Structured and audience-aware, careful about confidence and wording

fact_sheet.fact: The incident, designated SI-2024-045, was first detected on October 26, 2024, at 02:15 UTC.
The initial alert was an AWS GuardDuty finding for 'Anomalous API Usage' originating from IP address 198.51.100.72.
The incident was formally declared and escalated to the Cyber Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT) on October 26, 2024, at 03:00 UTC.
Forensic analysis indicates the threat actor, preliminarily identified as 'Cobalt Mirage', gained initial access on October 24, 2024, at approximately 19:40 UTC.
The initial access vector was the exploitation of vulnerability CVE-2024-3094 in a public-facing Jenkins server at host ci.stellarinnovations.net.
A malicious payload with SHA256 hash a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2 was deployed on the Jenkins server.
The threat actor established a command-and-control (C2) channel to the domain net-updater.org over TCP port 443.
Lateral movement was observed from the Jenkins server to the 'Orion Customer Data Platform' database server db-orion-prod-01.us-east-1.internal.
The threat actor authenticated to the database server using stolen credentials for the service account 'svc-jenkins-deploy'.
Data exfiltration was confirmed from the AWS S3 bucket 'stellar-orion-customer-backups' to the external IP address 203.0.113.55.
The 'Orion Customer Data Platform' contains Personally Identifiable Information (PII) for approximately 1.2 million customers of Stellar Innovations Inc.
The types of exfiltrated data confirmed to be exposed are customer full names, email addresses, and SHA-256 hashed phone numbers.
Financial data, such as credit card numbers, is stored in a separate, unaffected PCI-compliant environment and is not considered at risk from this incident.
The estimated volume of exfiltrated data is 75 GB, compressed into a single archive file named 'customer_data_full.tar.gz'.
As of 10:00 UTC on October 26, 2024, there is no evidence that production services for customers have been disrupted or rendered unavailable.
The compromised Jenkins server ci.stellarinnovations.net was isolated from the network on October 26, 2024, at 04:30 UTC.
The compromised service account 'svc-jenkins-deploy' had its credentials rotated and permissions revoked at 05:00 UTC on October 26, 2024.
An egress firewall rule was deployed at 05:15 UTC to block all outbound traffic to the C2 domain 'net-updater.org' and IP 203.0.113.55.
A full memory and disk image of the affected database server db-orion-prod-01 was captured for forensic analysis at 06:15 UTC.
The designated Incident Commander is Priya Sharma, Lead Incident Responder, reachable at priya.sharma@stellarinnovations.net.
The dedicated Slack channel for internal incident response coordination is #incident-si-2024-045.
The technical team provides written status updates every 60 minutes on the hour in the designated Slack channel.
A leadership briefing is scheduled via video conference with CEO Dr. Evelyn Reed for 14:00 UTC on October 26, 2024.
Security Program Manager Alex Chen is the sole designated communication liaison for the Legal and Leadership teams.
The official incident response log is maintained in the Confluence space 'CSIRT' under the page titled 'SI-2024-045 - Cobalt Mirage Incident'.
General Counsel David Miller was formally briefed on the incident at 07:00 UTC on October 26, 2024.
Stellar Innovations Inc. is subject to GDPR, and initial analysis confirms the exfiltrated data includes PII of at least 250,000 EU citizens.
The legal team has calculated the 72-hour GDPR notification deadline as October 29, 2024, at 02:15 UTC.
The external forensics firm 'CyberTrace Solutions' has been engaged under retainer; their point of contact is Mark Jennings.
A preliminary, non-public notification was made to the FBI's CyWatch division via liaison agent Sarah Jenkins at 08:00 UTC on October 26, 2024.

user_needs.description: What is the official incident designator, and what are the key timestamps for initial detection and formal declaration?
What was the specific technical alert that first triggered the investigation?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After learning when the incident was declared, the user would naturally want to know the specific technical event that started the process.

user_needs.description: What was the initial access vector and when is the earliest evidence of threat actor activity?
What indicators of compromise, such as malicious file hashes or C2 domains, have been identified?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Once the initial access vector is understood, the next logical technical question is about the specific tools and infrastructure the attacker used.

user_needs.description: What specific types of PII were exposed, and what is the total number of customers affected?
Was any financial data exposed or have any production services been disrupted?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After confirming PII was exposed, it's critical to clarify the scope by confirming what was *not* affected, such as financial data or service availability.

user_needs.description: What immediate containment actions have been taken regarding the compromised server and user account?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After understanding the full scope of the impact, the most pressing question for leadership and legal is what actions have been taken to stop the bleeding.

user_needs.description: Given that EU citizen data was exposed, what is our calculated 72-hour GDPR notification deadline?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Learning that customer PII was exfiltrated (N5) immediately triggers a need to understand regulatory obligations, making the GDPR deadline a highly predictable and critical follow-up.

user_needs.description: Who is the designated Incident Commander for this event?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning about the containment actions taken, the user will need to know who is leading the response effort to direct further questions or receive direction.

user_needs.description: What is the dedicated communication channel for the internal response team and when is the next leadership briefing scheduled?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Knowing who the Incident Commander is leads to questions about the communication structure they have established for the team and for leadership.

user_needs.description: Have we engaged any external forensics firms or notified law enforcement?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After understanding the internal containment actions, a common follow-up question is whether external expert resources or authorities have been brought in.
